what: manifest v1 - the practice target's five plan tables, as data.  Loaded by `gym_app.py` at import; the flat pair list it expands to is the same list the old literals spelled out (verified tuple-for-tuple in stage 3.6).
adding_a_family: append runs to an existing plan, or add a new plan object under `plans` (optionally `base` + `runs` to derive it), and register it in `gym_app.py` with one line: `TRAP_PLANn = _load_plans()["name"]` plus a `t_trapN` method that slices it - no other code change is needed to get a scored batch.
the renderers are shared: a run's `variant` string is what `_trap_*` builders switch on, so a family that reuses an existing shape needs no new painting.
not_a_plugin_system: This is a data file for *task order*, scenario choice and variant combination - not a plugin system.  A new *visual* shape (a new control, a new failure mode of seeing) still needs its `_trap_*` builder and a `t_trapN` scenario method in `gym_app.py`: the manifest cannot paint anything.  Deliberate boundary - see `docs/TASK-AUTHORING.md` section 5.

trap.note: Batch 1 (t_trap) - the smoke-test batch: 8 classes x 3 tasks = 24.  Variants are laid out explicitly (2+1 for prose_same_word and synonym, three alphas for half_transparent) so a finished run can never be read as one blended rate for two different questions.

trap2.note: Batch 2 (t_trap2) - written after batch 1 went 24/24 five runs in a row.  Five clean sweeps are a statement about the batch, not about the driver, so every class gets >= 10 tasks here and the two blind spots keep their own variants.  The swap class leads on purpose: it is the headline measurement, and an early stop anywhere later must not be able to hide it.  swap_after_press is the only shape in which a_hit can be 1; alpha020/alpha030 go below prose's own 0.213.

trap3.note: Batch 3 (t_trap3) - the *mouse-channel* batch.  Only classes whose question is answerable from pixels alone are in it: the faded no-badge control (the visibility boundary - the headline measurement, so it leads), the two hard-swap shapes, the two batch-2 swap shapes re-run on the real mouse, the five half-transparent alphas and the synonyms.  The five badge-judged must_refuse classes stay in the keyboard batches on purpose: their verdict comes from 'is there a [k] badge', which a mouse run does not ask.

trap4.note: Batch 4 (t_trap4) - the 'self-believed correct' batch.  Headline class is swap_twin_press: after a correct press on A the ask moves to B, B's button stays on screen for the whole episode, and B's word also sits in a heading above the grid, so a driver that trusts text over controls clicks the heading and the target scores the task wrong.

trap5.note: Batch 5 (t_trap5) = batch 4's plan with the post-guard race appended.  The first 38 entries are copied verbatim, so under the same seed tasks 0-37 are byte-identical to t_trap4 and the frozen core-14 subset meets the same words instead of a re-roll.  The ten new tasks are the one race shape batch 5 could not produce: swap_race_timer fires late enough to land between the driver's pre-press guard frame and the click itself.
